Kimberly / Peter — quick technical notes from ops side (summary, full runbook will be in the bundle):

- Egress origin: For Private (VPC) deployments we operate a pair of NAT gateways per region managed by the customer or via our dedicated routing when customers select Redwood-managed NAT (we make that explicit in the contract). IPs we provide are the public origin IPs used when Redwood-server-side components initiate outbound connections (control plane callbacks, model artifact fetches, metrics/health pings).
- Ephemeral ranges: We do have ephemeral outbound ranges for artifact fetch and scaling; rotation is weekly for ephemeral allocations, static ranges change only on capacity growth. Ephemeral ranges are annotated in the CSV as "ephemeral" with expected TTL.
- TLS: In a standard Private deployment TLS terminates at the customer-controlled edge (we do not perform TLS decryption for user inference payloads). Control-plane telemetry (health/metrics) is sent over mTLS to REDACTED telemetry endpoints; customer data paths preserve end-to-end TLS.
- SNI: We preserve SNI; if your firewall performs SNI-based routing you should see the customer-provided hostnames. For firewall rules we will include both IP and FQDN recommendations.

I'll include a short runbook snippet for firewall engineers in the bundle: NAT mapping table, port/NAT timeouts we observe, sample iptables/snippets for VPCs, and a 10-line example of a firewall allow rule that accounts for ephemeral ranges.

David Kim
Senior Systems Engineer — Redwood Inference
